newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank says bought $4.6 bln in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank says bought $4.6 bln in 1996.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Wednesday it bought a net $4.6 billion on the foreign exchange market since the start of the year to keep the exchange rate stable in the face of upward pressure on the peso.
The Philippines had been a recipient of strong inflows of foreign investments and remittances of overseas Filipinos, the bank said in a statement.

The peso was relatively stable in 1996, the Central Bank said, adding the currency had weakened less than 1/2 percent since January. It was at an average of 26.302 to the dollar on Tuesday compared with 26.214 at the start of the year.
Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said the stability of the peso was due to the economy's sound fundamentals and the strong commitment of authorities to maintain monetary stability.
The Central Bank's aggressive intervention in the foreign exchange market had, in turn, boosted the country's gross international reserves to $1.7 billion as of December 20, 1996, the statement said.

Similarly, foreign currency deposits of 48 commercial banks in the country reached a record $14.198 billion as of December 13, a 51 percent jump from the year-ago level of $9.43 billion, the Central Bank said.
